However, they can compromise customer privacy and safety as home layouts, sound, and imagery are analyzed through cloud-based AI (White 2025). • Smart outletsandsmart light bulbscan be operated remotely, or configured to turn on or off under certain conditions (timer, occupancy, etc). This can save energy if they are set up to reduce the time that energy is used. It can also increase safety, e.g. break-ins are less likely if the lights are turned on. Unlike these smart devices, legacy devices are not able to integrate with a building control system, or be operated remotely on-demand. A minimum level of observation and control can be achieved by adding smart plugs to legacy devices, but most devices do not automatically start tasks immediately upon being plugged in. 2.1.3 Control Systems Building control systems can monitor and control building loads. With these systems, buildings are kept within a specified range of parameters for occupant comfort and energy efficiency, and it is possible to take advantage of energy price incentives. In case of major grid events like high demand or outages, control systems can support the grid by implementing load management and serving as a flexible load. • Home Automation Systemscan enable flexible controls in residential buildings by tying smart appliances together. These systems can connect to utility programs and enable coordination of loads across a district of buildings. • Building Management and Automation Systemsin commercial buildings, also called BMS or BAS, provide the capability to integrate distributed sensing (e.g. temperature, occupancy, etc.) to monitor and control the time and amount of energy expended by major building loads, such as HVAC, and lighting. As commercial buildings are larger and more complex, these systems have to be able to manage a large number of devices. For instance, a large building typically has multiple thermal zones, but due to airflow between them, the system has to coordinate control across zones to achieve the desired temperature in each area. In addition, it may have to respond to varying factors, such as occupancy levels, infiltration rates, and solar heat gain, impacting parts of the building differently throughout the day. • Industrial Building Controlshave the biggest variation in systems as each industry has its own specific plug and process loads, and schedule requirements to account for.
